method: Repository-grounded adversarial audit updated after v12 step-level durable recovery, lease fencing, approval compare-and-set, hash-bound verification, verification-aware routing, governed-memory ablation, risk-adjusted autonomy, pilot-readiness truth gates, property/race probes, targeted mutation probes, and six-mode dynamic Roast.; v13 pilot convergence, isolated-lane validation, fail-closed readiness, and build-boundary audit

ratingScale.critical: Can invalidate security, data integrity, recoverability, or truthful operation.
ratingScale.high: Material production risk or major missing control.
ratingScale.medium: Important weakness with narrower blast radius or compensating controls.
ratingScale.low: Quality or maintainability issue with limited direct risk.

findings.title: Detached in-memory execution cannot survive process loss
findings.description: A feature-flagged durable envelope and SQLite durable primitives now exist, but granular step resume and active restart recovery remain incomplete.
findings.impact: Long-running or side-effecting jobs can disappear, duplicate, or remain permanently inconsistent after deployment, crash, or upgrade.
findings.recommendation: Complete native multi-process crash tests and replace the single-step envelope with granular checkpoints and fencing.
findings.acceptanceTest: Kill the worker at every checkpoint boundary and prove the run resumes exactly once with preserved ownership and evidence.

findings.title: Side effects lack persisted idempotency and atomic evidence
findings.description: The v9 portable core now persists deterministic side-effect receipts and proves crash replay without duplication. The production runner still lacks the SQLite transactional receipt, event, and audit integration.
findings.impact: A crash after a side effect but before acknowledgement can repeat irreversible work or create evidence that disagrees with reality.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the production runner to the portable contract with a SQLite compare-and-set lease and transactional outbox.
findings.acceptanceTest: Inject a crash after external success but before event commit and prove the retry does not repeat the effect.

findings.title: Deployment model conflicts with globally shared mutable data
findings.description: Authentication is multi-user, but policies, templates, and parts of audit/configuration are global rather than tenant-owned. Administrative restrictions reduce some exposure but do not establish a complete tenancy model.
findings.impact: One user can be affected by another user's global configuration or data; future multi-user deployment risks cross-tenant leakage and confused authority.
findings.recommendation: Choose and enforce either explicit single-owner mode or workspace/tenant ownership across every mutable record and query.
findings.acceptanceTest: Create two tenants and prove every read, write, audit, template, skill, run, and artifact is isolated under adversarial identifiers.

findings.title: HTTP and provider endpoints allowed server-side request forgery
findings.description: User-influenced HTTP and provider base URLs previously had no private-network, loopback, metadata, DNS-rebinding, or redirect boundary.
findings.impact: An agent could probe internal services, cloud metadata, or local control planes.
findings.recommendation: Keep destination and redirect validation, DNS resolution checks, and explicit local-model exceptions under policy.
findings.acceptanceTest: Run the egress suite against loopback, RFC1918, link-local, metadata, IPv6, encoded addresses, mixed DNS answers, and redirect chains.

findings.title: Invalid or cyclic plans could be reported as completed
findings.description: The original scheduler could reach no-ready-step state while unfinished nodes remained and still finish the run successfully.
findings.impact: A structurally impossible plan could produce a false success signal and misleading evidence.
findings.recommendation: Retain preflight plan validation and fail closed when unfinished work has no executable node.
findings.acceptanceTest: Test duplicate nodes, unknown edges, self-dependencies, cycles, excessive steps, and runtime deadlock.

findings.title: No tested sovereign backup and restore path
findings.description: The v10 package creates a consistent SQLite snapshot, encrypts it with scrypt and AES-256-GCM, verifies integrity and required tables, restores atomically, preserves an overwritten database, and includes positive and negative restore tests.
findings.impact: Loss or corruption of the SQLite database, keys, artifacts, or model configuration can be unrecoverable.
findings.recommendation: Run periodic clean-deployment RTO/RPO drills and store the passphrase separately from the backup.
findings.acceptanceTest: Restore the encrypted backup into a clean target, verify the sentinel data and database checks, then prove wrong-key, tamper, and unauthorized-overwrite attempts fail closed.

findings.title: Drizzle ORM remains on a version with a high-severity advisory
findings.description: The current dependency range resolves below the audited fixed line identified by npm audit for identifier-related SQL injection.
findings.impact: Unsafe identifier construction in affected paths can turn application input into SQL structure rather than data.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade Drizzle ORM to a supported non-vulnerable release, regenerate/migrate safely, and execute database integration tests.
findings.acceptanceTest: npm audit contains no high advisory for Drizzle and all migration/query/integration tests pass on a clean install.

findings.title: Any authenticated user could mutate global policy
findings.description: The policy update path previously had an ineffective administrative check while changing system-wide policy.
findings.impact: A normal user could weaken approval requirements for all users.
findings.recommendation: Retain explicit administrative authorization and later tenant-scope policy records.
findings.acceptanceTest: A non-admin receives a denial and cannot change persisted policy; an authorized admin creates an attributable audit event.

findings.title: Skill identifiers enabled cross-user prompt access or attachment
findings.description: Direct skill fetch and agent skill replacement did not consistently verify ownership.
findings.impact: A user who guessed an identifier could read or attach another user's procedural prompt material.
findings.recommendation: Keep owner/built-in checks on both reads and relationship writes.
findings.acceptanceTest: Attempt direct reads and attachment with another user's skill identifier and prove denial without existence leakage.

findings.title: New or empty agents inherited every tool
findings.description: Agent creation and runtime fallback could translate absent or empty tool configuration into the full registry.
findings.impact: A minimally configured agent could unexpectedly gain network or write authority.
findings.recommendation: Keep an explicit low-risk default allowlist and treat an empty list as no capabilities.
findings.acceptanceTest: Create agents with omitted and empty tool lists; prove only documented tools can execute.

findings.title: Catch-all policy allowed medium-risk actions automatically
findings.description: The default policy set included a broad catch-all automatic path that weakened the documented fallback behavior.
findings.impact: Risky actions could bypass human review despite the UI implying otherwise.
findings.recommendation: Keep fail-closed fallback policy and require explicit, narrow auto-approval rules.
findings.acceptanceTest: Unknown and medium/high-risk actions resolve to human review or denial in policy tests.

findings.title: Runs and approvals have no complete wall-clock deadline model
findings.description: Runs now accept explicit wall-clock deadlines and output/context budgets; approvals persist an expiry timestamp and are expired by local timers and boot recovery. A durable timer service and restart-safe continuation are still absent.
findings.impact: A run can occupy resources indefinitely or remain pending forever after user abandonment.
findings.recommendation: Add persisted deadlines, timeout ownership, cancellation propagation, and deterministic terminal states.
findings.acceptanceTest: Advance a fake clock across model, tool, approval, and run deadlines and prove exact terminal events and released leases.

findings.title: Run event sequence allocation is race-prone
findings.description: Run event sequence allocation and insertion now execute under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a unique run/sequence constraint and an atomic outbox record. Native multi-process contention tests remain blocked in this environment.
findings.impact: Concurrent writers can duplicate or reorder sequence numbers and break replay evidence.
findings.recommendation: Use a transactionally allocated sequence or append-only event table with a unique run/sequence constraint and retry.
findings.acceptanceTest: Run concurrent appenders and prove contiguous unique ordering under load and injected transaction retries.

findings.title: Audit hash-chain append is race-prone and not externally anchored
findings.description: Audit hash-chain read, hash calculation, append, and outbox insertion now run in one immediate transaction. External anchoring and native concurrent-writer tests remain.
findings.impact: Concurrent events can fork the chain; a database administrator can rewrite the entire chain and recompute hashes.
findings.recommendation: Serialize append, add uniqueness, sign periodic roots, and optionally export roots to independent storage.
findings.acceptanceTest: Generate concurrent audit writes, verify one linear chain, then mutate history and prove signed-root verification fails.

findings.title: Disabled provider configurations were still eligible
findings.description: Provider activation status was not consistently enforced during dispatch or provider tests.
findings.impact: An operator could believe a provider was disabled while the system still sent data to it.
findings.recommendation: Retain enabled checks at every provider resolution boundary.
findings.acceptanceTest: Disable each provider and prove dispatch, health test, and fallback routing never contact it.

findings.title: Database migration failure was tolerated
findings.description: Migration errors were logged but startup could continue against an unknown schema.
findings.impact: The application could write incompatible data or fail later in less diagnosable ways.
findings.recommendation: Keep startup fail-closed for required schema migrations.
findings.acceptanceTest: Force a migration failure and prove the process refuses readiness without serving mutation routes.

findings.title: Fetched content remains a prompt-injection channel
findings.description: Fetched data is now labeled untrusted and egress-limited, but untrusted text still enters model context without a fully enforced authority separation or content transformation policy.
findings.impact: A malicious page can attempt to override instructions, induce tool use, or exfiltrate context.
findings.recommendation: Separate data from instructions, apply trust labels in the internal protocol, and require policy authorization independent of model text.
findings.acceptanceTest: Use adversarial fetched pages that request secrets and destructive tools; prove zero authority escalation and no protected-context leakage.

findings.title: Native database integration tests cannot run in the constrained environment
findings.description: The safe install deliberately skips native post-install scripts, leaving better-sqlite3 unavailable for three database-backed suites.
findings.impact: Critical approval expiry, audit, and runner integration behavior is not independently executed in this environment.
findings.recommendation: Run the blocked suites on an approved clean Linux CI image with pinned Node headers and a trusted prebuilt/native toolchain.
findings.acceptanceTest: All database suites pass from a clean lockfile install and publish logs, environment digest, and database reset evidence.

findings.title: Production build did not complete end-to-end in the audit environment
findings.description: The production build compiles and completes type validation, but page-data collection cannot load the absent better-sqlite3 native binding in the constrained environment.
findings.impact: A source-level and compile-level green result does not prove deployable application startup or route data collection.
findings.recommendation: Run the build with the verified native binding on a trusted CI or development host, then execute startup and browser E2E gates.
findings.acceptanceTest: A clean install completes the production build, starts the server, and passes Playwright without hidden network or native-binding errors.

findings.title: User data export, correction, and deletion are not implemented end-to-end
findings.description: User export, password-confirmed deletion, owned-data cascade, governed-memory correction/deletion, and logical audit redaction overlays are implemented. Native end-to-end deletion, backup propagation, and legal retention validation remain.
findings.impact: Users cannot exercise data rights reliably and deleted data may survive in logs, artifacts, or backups.
findings.recommendation: Implement data inventory-backed export and deletion workflows with tombstone/backup semantics and audit evidence.
findings.acceptanceTest: Create a user with all data classes, export it, delete it, search every primary/derived store, restore an older backup, and prove policy-compliant handling.

findings.title: Custom templates are globally visible and mutable
findings.description: Custom templates now carry an owner identifier; listing and creation expose only built-in templates plus the authenticated user's templates.
findings.impact: Private workflows or proprietary prompts can be exposed or changed across users.
findings.recommendation: Separate immutable built-ins from tenant-owned custom templates and scope every query.
findings.acceptanceTest: Two-user route tests prove private templates cannot be listed, read, updated, or referenced cross-tenant.

findings.title: Audit access is restricted but audit data remains globally modeled
findings.description: The route now restricts entries to administrators, but audit rows lack a complete tenant/workspace ownership model and delegated audit roles.
findings.impact: A global administrator becomes a high-value data aggregation point and tenant-level audit cannot be safely delegated.
findings.recommendation: Add tenant/workspace dimensions and explicit audit-reader roles while preserving system-level security audit separation.
findings.acceptanceTest: Tenant auditors see only their workspace; system auditors see redacted cross-tenant metadata under separate authorization.

findings.title: Registration remains open with weak abuse controls
findings.description: Registration now bootstraps only the first administrator by default, remains closed afterward unless explicitly enabled, supports an invite token, enforces a twelve-character minimum, and uses rate limiting without trusting proxy headers by default.
findings.impact: An exposed installation can be populated by unauthorized users and amplified against local or paid model resources.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit registration mode, invitation/first-owner bootstrap, stronger password checks, throttling, and non-enumerating responses.
findings.acceptanceTest: Unauthenticated registration is denied in closed mode; invite reuse, enumeration, weak passwords, and burst attempts fail safely.

findings.title: Secret encryption lacks documented rotation and context binding
findings.description: Provider secrets now use versioned AES-GCM records, HKDF purpose separation, and user/provider context binding with legacy decryption compatibility. Automated rotation, revocation, and custody recovery are not complete.
findings.impact: A leaked master key or ciphertext relocation can expose all provider credentials with limited recovery options.
findings.recommendation: Introduce key IDs, rotation, AEAD associated data, scoped decrypt authority, secure backup handling, and revocation drills.
findings.acceptanceTest: Rotate from key A to B without downtime, prove old ciphertext migration, reject swapped record context, and restore credentials securely.

findings.title: Run creation has no client idempotency contract
findings.description: Run creation accepts a user-scoped Idempotency-Key, serializes create-or-reuse under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, rejects key reuse with a different request, and has a unique database constraint. Native concurrent API tests remain blocked.
findings.impact: Network retries or double clicks can duplicate expensive or destructive work.
findings.recommendation: Accept scoped idempotency keys, persist request/result hashes, and return the original run for safe retries.
findings.acceptanceTest: Send the same request concurrently and repeatedly; prove exactly one run and a deterministic replay response.

findings.title: Approval expiry is not owned by a durable timer
findings.description: Approval expiry is persisted and enforced by local wait timers and startup sweeping, but no independent durable timer worker owns expiry while the application is offline.
findings.impact: Expired approvals can remain pending or resume ambiguously, blocking work and weakening policy guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Persist approval deadlines and let a durable worker own expiry, cancellation, and notification.
findings.acceptanceTest: Restart before and after expiry and prove one deterministic expired transition and no later execution.

findings.title: Restart semantics for pending approvals are incomplete
findings.description: A serializable revision-checked approval wait contract now proves one-decision and expiry semantics, but the active runner still cannot resume it after restart.
findings.impact: An approved action may never resume or may be reissued incorrectly after restart.
findings.recommendation: Persist the wait contract, durable timer, continuation pointer, and requeue behavior in the active runner.
findings.acceptanceTest: Restart with a pending approval, decide it from another process, and prove the exact continuation resumes once.

findings.title: Configured maximum plan size was not enforced
findings.description: The planner schema previously accepted plans beyond the configured step limit.
findings.impact: A model could create runaway work graphs and consume disproportionate resources.
findings.recommendation: Keep max-step enforcement at parse/validation time.
findings.acceptanceTest: Generate plans at limit, limit+1, and extreme sizes; prove bounded parse time and clear rejection.

findings.title: Tool iteration exhaustion could be treated as success
findings.description: A step could leave the model still requesting tools after the loop budget but continue toward completion.
findings.impact: Incomplete or looping work could be presented as successful.
findings.recommendation: Fail the step and run with explicit budget-exhausted evidence.
findings.acceptanceTest: Use a model fixture that always requests another tool and prove deterministic failure at the configured limit.

findings.title: Usage accounting could double-count tokens
findings.description: Token usage could be recorded both through provider events and response usage aggregation.
findings.impact: Cost, capacity, and model-routing decisions could be based on inflated telemetry.
findings.recommendation: Use one authoritative accounting path with reconciliation fields.
findings.acceptanceTest: Replay a response with provider usage events and summary usage; prove totals equal the provider bill once.

findings.title: Rejected approval did not close the tool evidence chain
findings.description: A rejected action produced a model-facing result but no matching tool.result event.
findings.impact: Evidence reconstruction reported an unmatched call and could not explain the human decision path.
findings.recommendation: Emit a terminal tool result representing rejection without executing the tool.
findings.acceptanceTest: Reject an approval and prove call/result pairing, no side effect, and visible human-decision evidence.

findings.title: Prompts and objectives are duplicated into persistent evidence without minimization
findings.description: Full system prompts and run objectives are no longer duplicated into run-start events or audit payloads; hashes and character counts are stored instead. The objective remains once in the run record because it is operational input, and broader retention controls remain.
findings.impact: Sensitive business data can persist longer and in more stores than users expect.
findings.recommendation: Store references/hashes and redacted summaries by default; define an explicit secure evidence retention mode for full content.
findings.acceptanceTest: Insert known sensitive markers and prove default logs/events/audit omit them while authorized artifact storage remains traceable.

findings.title: Artifact writes had no practical size ceiling
findings.description: The write-artifact tool accepted unbounded content.
findings.impact: A model could exhaust memory, disk, database capacity, or UI rendering.
findings.recommendation: Keep a documented byte cap and later add streaming/object storage where justified.
findings.acceptanceTest: Attempt boundary, boundary+1, and multibyte payloads and prove exact size enforcement.

findings.title: Policy regular expressions can create denial of service
findings.description: Policy patterns pass a bounded safe-regex compiler that rejects oversized expressions, backreferences, lookarounds, nested quantifiers, repeated wildcards, and malformed patterns before evaluation.
findings.impact: Catastrophic backtracking can block the Node.js event loop during authorization.
findings.recommendation: Use constrained glob/pattern semantics or safe-regex validation and bounded evaluation.
findings.acceptanceTest: Submit known pathological expressions and long inputs; prove bounded latency or rejection.

findings.title: Rate limiting is process-local and trusts client forwarding headers
findings.description: Forwarding headers are ignored unless proxy trust is explicitly enabled. Rate-limit state remains process-local and therefore is not a distributed production control.
findings.impact: Attackers can bypass limits across workers/restarts or by rotating forged header values.
findings.recommendation: Use authenticated principal/workspace keys and a shared limiter or documented single-process boundary; configure trusted proxies explicitly.
findings.acceptanceTest: Exercise multiple workers, restarts, spoofed headers, users, and IPs; prove the intended global and per-user budget.

findings.title: Security headers improved but CSP remains absent
findings.description: The application now sends a Content Security Policy and baseline headers. The compatibility policy still permits inline scripts and styles, and browser-level enforcement tests remain.
findings.impact: A future injection bug has fewer browser-side containment barriers.
findings.recommendation: Add nonce/hash-based CSP, report-only rollout, and route tests without breaking Next.js runtime behavior.
findings.acceptanceTest: Production responses include the approved CSP and Playwright confirms no required script/style violations.

findings.title: Source lint is intentionally shallow and build ignores ESLint
findings.description: Build no longer suppresses ESLint and the non-interactive source lint checks merge markers, dangerous directives, dynamic code execution, malformed JSON, and client/server boundaries. A full semantic ESLint ruleset remains absent.
findings.impact: Common correctness, React, security, and accessibility defects can pass CI.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a pinned non-interactive ESLint configuration plus targeted security/accessibility rules and keep the fast scanner as an additional gate.
findings.acceptanceTest: A clean install runs lint non-interactively; seeded violations fail with stable diagnostics.

findings.title: No generated SBOM, model inventory, or build provenance
findings.description: The release pipeline generates a CycloneDX SBOM, license inventory, model inventory, and source-tree build provenance with hashes.
findings.impact: Operators cannot reliably identify vulnerable components, licenses, models, plugins, or reproduce the artifact.
findings.recommendation: Generate CycloneDX/SPDX, license inventory, model/plugin hashes, and build provenance during release.
findings.acceptanceTest: The extracted ZIP contains validated inventories matching the lockfile and shipped artifacts, signed or hashed in the release manifest.

findings.title: Observability lacks traces, SLOs, and capacity evidence
findings.description: A local metrics endpoint now reports status counts, latency percentiles, token usage, approval expiry, outbox backlog, durable-job state, and SLO evaluations. Cross-boundary traces, energy measurement, historical capacity series, and telemetry retention remain.
findings.impact: Operators cannot answer why work is slow, expensive, failing, or saturating resources.
findings.recommendation: Add redacted trace correlation, metrics, usage reconciliation, queue measures, SLOs, and local dashboards.
findings.acceptanceTest: A benchmark run yields traceable p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, failure classes, token/cost totals, and an SLO verdict.

findings.title: Governed memory architecture is documentation-only
findings.description: Governed memory is implemented and integrated into prompt assembly with owner filtering, expiry, token budgets, quarantine, provenance labeling, corrections, and deletion.
findings.impact: Long-running agents either forget important context or accumulate untrusted, stale, contradictory, or cross-user material.
findings.recommendation: Maintain ablation and poisoning evaluations before expanding automatic memory creation.
findings.acceptanceTest: Create contradictory, expired, private, corrected, and deleted memories; prove scoring, provenance, isolation, and removal behavior.

findings.title: Provider selection is not a measured capability router
findings.description: Model capability profiles, hard eligibility constraints, deterministic utility scoring, explicit fallback, no-eligible failure, persistence, API control, and run-level rationale are implemented.
findings.impact: Critical work can be dispatched by static configuration rather than demonstrated fitness.
findings.recommendation: Populate profiles through repeatable benchmark runs and invalidate stale evaluations.
findings.acceptanceTest: Given constrained tasks and unavailable models, route to the Pareto-eligible candidate or return no-eligible-model without silent downgrade.

findings.title: Test portfolio is too narrow for the threat and failure model
findings.description: The safe portfolio now includes lifecycle, evidence, egress, durable execution, backup/restore, memory, regex, tool-schema, metrics, context-budget, graph, crypto, and policy tests. Native database, browser, accessibility, load, and broad fault-injection suites remain incomplete.
findings.impact: The system can pass 47 safe tests while remaining unsafe under realistic operation.
findings.recommendation: Build layered adversarial and fault-injection suites tied to every high/critical finding.
findings.acceptanceTest: Each high/critical finding has a failing regression before repair and a passing independent verification after repair.

findings.title: End-to-end tests are brittle smoke checks
findings.description: The Playwright suite now uses operator-supplied credentials, semantic readiness conditions, and coverage for run evidence, agent evaluation, and governed-memory lifecycle. Isolated database fixtures, repeated parallel/serial execution, accessibility assertions, and measured flake-rate evidence remain.
findings.impact: The suite is materially less brittle, but shared-state and unexecuted browser coverage can still conceal authorization, recovery, accessibility, or concurrency regressions.
findings.recommendation: Add per-run isolated databases and users, deterministic fixture teardown, accessibility checks, authorization negatives, restart recovery, and repeated serial/parallel flake measurement.
findings.acceptanceTest: Run the E2E suite repeatedly in serial and parallel modes against isolated state, including accessibility, authorization, offline, and recovery cases, with a bounded measured flake rate.

findings.title: Seed workflow is destructive and includes known demo credentials
findings.description: The seed refuses to run unless a destructive-seed flag is set, requires an operator-supplied twelve-character demo password, and no longer contains fallback application secrets or prints credentials.
findings.impact: Running it in the wrong environment can destroy data or create an easily guessed account.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit development/test environment, random ephemeral credentials, targeted fixture cleanup, and destructive confirmation guards.
findings.acceptanceTest: Attempt seed in production mode and against a non-empty protected database; prove hard refusal and no mutation.

findings.title: Evidence percentage measures structure, not truth
findings.description: The UI originally risked presenting event-shape completeness as overall evidence quality. It is now labeled structural coverage, but semantic correctness and verifier independence remain separate unfinished controls.
findings.impact: Users can over-trust a complete-looking ledger even when outputs are wrong or self-verified.
findings.recommendation: Keep structural labeling and add claim-level evidence, verifier identity, reproducibility, contradiction, and semantic evaluation.
findings.acceptanceTest: Show a structurally complete but deliberately false run and prove the UI does not label it verified.

findings.title: Most canonical capabilities remain blocked or unimplemented
findings.description: v9 and v10 implement durable contracts, SQLite persistence primitives, transactional outbox, governed memory, encrypted restore, lifecycle controls, observability, data export/deletion, budgets, and release provenance. Production worker cutover, measured routing, delegated identity, and full native/browser verification remain.
findings.impact: Documentation volume can be mistaken for platform maturity, obscuring the implementation gap.
findings.recommendation: Expose implemented-versus-designed status prominently and execute dependency-unblocking vertical slices rather than adding parallel documents.
findings.acceptanceTest: A release dashboard derives status from code/test evidence and cannot count designed-only tasks as delivered capability.

findings.title: SQLite and web-process topology limit safe scale and failover
findings.description: SQLite now has immediate-transaction serialization, persisted durable schemas, a repository-owned adapter, outbox leases, and migration checks. The web process still launches the production runner and there is no tested worker fleet or failover topology.
findings.impact: Multi-process deployment, failover, concurrent writers, and horizontal scaling can corrupt assumptions or lose work.
findings.recommendation: Define supported single-node limits, separate durable worker execution, and introduce a tested persistence profile before scaling out.
findings.acceptanceTest: Run load and failover tests at documented limits; unsupported topologies must fail configuration validation.

findings.title: No tested Content Security Policy
findings.description: A CSP is configured and scanned, but it retains unsafe-inline compatibility directives and has not passed browser-level nonce, third-party, or violation-report testing.
findings.impact: Cross-site scripting impact is not meaningfully contained at the browser policy layer.
findings.recommendation: Design and roll out report-only then enforced CSP with route-level automated checks.
findings.acceptanceTest: All production pages load under enforced CSP with no unauthorized script, style, frame, connect, image, or font source.

findings.title: Tool arguments are not uniformly governed by explicit versioned schemas
findings.description: Tools declare versioned schemas and capabilities; arguments are validated, allowlists enforced, and execution is bounded by timeout and output size.
findings.impact: Malformed, oversized, ambiguous, or injected arguments can reach tool implementations inconsistently.
findings.recommendation: Add OS-level isolation for high-risk tools and maintain mutation tests for schema bypass.
findings.acceptanceTest: Fuzz every tool with invalid types, extra fields, oversized values, Unicode edge cases, and schema-version mismatch.

findings.title: Context and output budgets are incomplete
findings.description: Run requests now bound context and output tokens; context assembly deterministically preserves mandatory messages and recent complete segments under budget. Adaptive stopping, cache isolation, and omission-quality benchmarks remain.
findings.impact: Long histories or retrieved content can crowd out policy/current facts, increase cost, and degrade correctness.
findings.recommendation: Implement mandatory-context reservation, measured selection, output ceilings, and bounded planner/critic/verifier stopping.
findings.acceptanceTest: Run adversarial long-context cases and prove mandatory policy/current code facts survive while cost and latency remain within budget.

findings.title: Stale workers could commit after lease takeover when identity was reused
findings.description: Durable mutations previously checked worker identity and lease time but did not bind commits to a monotonically increasing fencing token. A restarted worker using the same identity could race a newer lease holder.
findings.impact: Split-brain workers could overwrite checkpoints or complete a job after losing authority, invalidating exactly-once and recovery claims.
findings.recommendation: Require a fencing token on every lease-bound mutation and reject stale tokens in memory and SQLite adapters.
findings.acceptanceTest: Acquire a lease twice with the same worker identity after expiry; token 1 must be rejected and token 2 must commit.

findings.title: Approval resolution lacked a cross-process compare-and-set revision
findings.description: The active approval row had a status but no revision. Competing processes could both observe pending before one committed a terminal decision.
findings.impact: A stale operator action or concurrent process could overwrite or contradict the authoritative human decision.
findings.recommendation: Persist an approval revision and update terminal status only when id, prior status, and revision all match. Return a conflict to stale clients.
findings.acceptanceTest: Two resolutions using the same expected revision must yield one successful transition and one approval_revision_conflict.

findings.title: Verification decisions were not immutably bound to tested source and release artifacts
findings.description: Run evidence and human review existed, but there was no immutable attestation binding requirement revision, source tree, test output, artifact, builder, verifier, and release candidate.
findings.impact: A verification label could outlive or refer to different code and test evidence, creating false release confidence.
findings.recommendation: Create hash-bound verification attestations, reject builder/verifier identity collisions, and expose absent verification in the interface.
findings.acceptanceTest: Changing any bound field must invalidate the evidence hash; self-verification must be rejected.

findings.title: Runtime calm could be mistaken for release or pilot readiness
findings.description: Operational metrics showed local state but did not explicitly gate build, native tests, browser E2E, accessibility, restart recovery, tenant isolation, or extracted-package evidence.
findings.impact: An operator could interpret zero failures in an empty or lightly used system as evidence that the release was pilot-ready.
findings.recommendation: Add a conservative evidence gate that treats unknown release evidence as blocking and separates runtime health from release classification.
findings.acceptanceTest: Healthy empty metrics with unknown release facts must remain DEVELOPMENT ONLY; controlled pilot requires every hard fact.

findings.title: Model routing did not distinguish verification quality or unhealthy candidates
findings.description: The measured router scored planning and coding capabilities but lacked an explicit verifier-quality signal and health state.
findings.impact: Verification tasks could select a strong builder but weak reviewer, or choose an unavailable model if other metrics were attractive.
findings.recommendation: Record verification quality and health, apply task-class weighting, and reject unavailable candidates as a hard constraint.
findings.acceptanceTest: A verification task must select the eligible high-verification model and reject an unavailable higher-scoring model.

findings.title: Active approval waits were process-local and could not resume after restart
findings.description: The approval row survived, but the active model/tool continuation originally lived in process memory. v13 adds deterministic continuation keys, durable pause/requeue, revision compare-and-set, expiry, and checkpoint metadata for the bounded pilot path.
findings.impact: A restart during a risky action could leave the run permanently waiting or tempt an operator to repeat a side effect.
findings.recommendation: Execute native restart integration in the isolated lane and prove the exact approved step resumes once after process replacement.
findings.acceptanceTest: Persist a pending approval, terminate the process, restart, resolve the expected revision, and prove one side effect and one terminal durable state.

findings.title: Pilot resources lacked a complete tenant and workspace boundary
findings.description: v13 persists tenant, workspace, owner, and visibility across pilot resources and centralizes personal-scope resolution, but full multi-process and browser authorization testing is pending.
findings.impact: Resource identifiers could cross user or workspace boundaries even when individual routes appeared owner-filtered.
findings.recommendation: Run native cross-tenant API, search, artifact, approval, verification, export, backup, and restore tests, including mutations that remove predicates.
findings.acceptanceTest: Every cross-tenant read and write must fail, and removing one tenant predicate must make the suite fail.

findings.title: Pilot readiness could be implied by static or missing evidence
findings.description: v13 derives pilot readiness from run, durable job, receipt, approval, model, memory, capability, artifact, reconciliation, verification, and release evidence. Unknown evidence is blocking.
findings.impact: Operators could interpret an incomplete checklist or completed run as proof that the release was safe for pilot use.
findings.recommendation: Keep fail-closed evidence semantics and regression tests for every unknown gate.
findings.acceptanceTest: Removing any mandatory evidence item must change the run to blocked and identify the missing evidence.

findings.title: Database initialization during module import broke production build discovery
findings.description: The database was opened eagerly when API modules were imported during Next.js page-data collection. v13 opens SQLite lazily on first real database operation and forces authenticated application rendering to remain dynamic.
findings.impact: A clean source build required a native runtime binding even when no database query was executed, preventing reproducible packaging and hiding build/runtime boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Retain lazy initialization and verify the complete build in both source-safe and native CI lanes.
findings.acceptanceTest: Import the database module without a native binding and complete `next build` without opening SQLite.

findings.title: Native persistence validation is unavailable on the protected host
findings.description: v14 runs the complete persistence suite through Node 22 built-in SQLite without downloading or building a new binary. The better-sqlite3 native lane remains available in pinned CI but is not locally proven.
findings.impact: SQLite transactions, multi-process races, migrations, durable approval restart, and production runtime behavior are not locally proven.
findings.recommendation: Run the pinned isolated validation workflow and attach dependency provenance, native results, migrations, build, and resource metrics.
findings.acceptanceTest: The isolated lane must install from lockfile, run all native suites, and publish machine-readable evidence with exact package and binary provenance.

findings.title: Browser, accessibility, and visual regression gates are not executed locally
findings.description: Chromium is installed, but organization-managed policy sets URLBlocklist to ["*"], blocking localhost before application navigation. The managed policy was not modified or bypassed.
findings.impact: Keyboard, focus, responsive, accessibility, restart, reconciliation, and operator-truth behavior are not browser-verified.
findings.recommendation: Execute Chromium, Firefox, mobile, accessibility, and visual regression in the pinned disposable CI lane.
findings.acceptanceTest: All pilot browser scenarios must pass with screenshots, traces, accessibility results, and responsive evidence.

findings.title: Final verification is not yet independently bound to the released ZIP hash
findings.description: v13 includes a hash-bound verifier that rejects incomplete evidence, but no operationally separate verifier has accepted a final archive after native and browser gates.
findings.impact: The builder could package source that differs from tested evidence or overstate readiness.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the release, execute all isolated gates, bind evidence to the archive hash, and run a distinct verifier invocation that attempts rejection.
findings.acceptanceTest: A distinct verifier identity must accept the exact final ZIP SHA-256 with all required evidence hashes and no hidden critical limitation.

findings.title: Live remote model conversations remain outside restart-safe pilot execution
findings.description: The bounded pilot supports simulation and local artifact generation. Remote provider dialogue state is not serialized as durable model intents and immutable response references.
findings.impact: A restart during a live remote model interaction can require re-execution, consume additional cost, or produce a non-equivalent response.
findings.recommendation: Deny live-provider pilot execution until model request intents, response references, replay policy, cost accounting, and privacy scope are durable.
findings.acceptanceTest: Terminate before and after a remote response and prove deterministic continuation or explicit reconciliation without silent re-request.

findings.title: Runtime migration discovery applied only the first declared schema change
findings.description: The legacy migration journal listed only 0000 even though later SQL migrations existed. Runtime startup therefore could create an outdated schema while source validation merely counted files.
findings.impact: Production startup could omit durable, memory, tenancy, verification, and approval columns, creating runtime failures and misleading release evidence.
findings.recommendation: Keep ordered SQL files canonical, persist each filename and SHA-256, and reject migration drift.
findings.acceptanceTest: Apply all migrations to a clean database, rerun idempotently, and fail after modifying a historical migration.

findings.title: Static generation inherited an unbounded host CPU count
findings.description: Next.js inferred a very large CPU count in the container and spawned excessive static-generation workers.
findings.impact: Builds could stall, exhaust memory, or interfere with other workloads on high-core-count hosts.
findings.recommendation: Keep explicit bounded build concurrency and record build duration and route metrics.
findings.acceptanceTest: Complete the production build with two workers and a successful exit.

findings.title: Demo seed referenced tenant and workspace identifiers without creating the scope rows
findings.description: The seeded runs carried personal tenant and workspace identifiers while the tenants, workspaces, and memberships tables remained empty.
findings.impact: Demo and E2E state could appear scoped while lacking the membership records used by backend authorization.
findings.recommendation: Create the personal pilot scope before seeding scoped agents or runs.
findings.acceptanceTest: Seed a clean database and verify tenant, workspace, membership, run, approval, and artifact scope survive backup and restore.

findings.title: The local browser executable is governed by a deny-all URL policy
findings.description: The installed Chromium returns ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR for localhost because its managed URLBlocklist contains a wildcard deny rule.
findings.impact: Browser E2E, keyboard, responsive, offline, accessibility, and visual-regression claims cannot be made from this host.
findings.recommendation: Execute the pinned browser lane in a disposable CI worker and retain the local block as a release blocker.
findings.acceptanceTest: The same frozen candidate passes Chromium browser, accessibility, offline, and responsive tests in the disposable lane.

findings.title: Restore interruption after target displacement lacked a rollback proof
findings.description: The restore implementation had rollback code, but no deterministic kill-point proved that the original target is restored after displacement and before commit.
findings.impact: An interrupted restore could have been claimed atomic without evidence at the most dangerous boundary.
findings.recommendation: Retain explicit fault injection and regression coverage around target displacement.
findings.acceptanceTest: Inject failure immediately after displacement and verify the original target bytes remain available.

findings.title: Full-process outbound network behavior is not independently audited
findings.description: The sovereign network guard proves declared adapter policy, but no packet- or syscall-level audit has observed the complete application during startup, build, workflow execution, and shutdown with outbound traffic denied.
findings.impact: An undeclared dependency or library call could escape the application-level guard and invalidate air-gap claims.
findings.recommendation: Extend process attribution to Windows and an unrestricted browser/model lane; increase sampling or add firewall event evidence.
findings.acceptanceTest: The full pilot workflow records zero unexpected remote connection across application, browser, model, and child processes.

findings.title: No real local generative model artifact has been benchmarked
findings.description: The deterministic local runtime proves contracts and zero-key orchestration, while the medium local model is only a hardware profile and was not downloaded or executed.
findings.impact: Model sovereignty, task quality, tool reliability, memory behavior, latency, and hardware feasibility remain unproven for a useful generative workload.
findings.recommendation: Benchmark at least one license-reviewed local model artifact in a disposable environment and bind its hash, runtime, quality, memory, latency, and energy evidence to the registry.
findings.acceptanceTest: A real local model completes the sovereign golden workflow and adversarial structured-output tasks without commercial keys.

findings.title: Energy-aware scheduling uses estimates rather than measured hardware data
findings.description: The placement and energy policy contracts are implemented, but power, thermal, load, and task-energy values are synthetic estimates.
findings.impact: Energy-saving, thermal-protection, and local-versus-remote break-even decisions may be materially wrong on target hardware.
findings.recommendation: Collect repeated wall-power or trusted telemetry measurements for idle, model load, inference, retrieval, backup, and restore.
findings.acceptanceTest: Measured profiles include confidence intervals and alter routing only within validated bounds.

findings.title: Clean offline installation still depends on an unbuilt dependency bundle
findings.description: The source release and signed update are self-contained, but a new machine still requires JavaScript packages, system prerequisites, browser artifacts, and any real model artifact from external sources.
findings.impact: Loss of public registries or model hubs prevents clean installation and disaster recovery onto replacement hardware.
findings.recommendation: Package or separately verify a compatible Node runtime and prove installation on the target clean machine.
findings.acceptanceTest: A clean target installs source, runtime, dependencies, browser and model artifacts with public registries denied.

findings.title: Signed air-gap bundles were replayable and ignored local key revocation
findings.description: Signature validation alone accepted a copied task or result repeatedly and could not reject a compromised node key.
findings.impact: An attacker or operator error could repeat bounded work, duplicate local writes, or accept evidence from a revoked offline node.
findings.recommendation: Retain purpose-scoped trust checks and a durable replay ledger at the acceptance boundary.
findings.acceptanceTest: A new process instance rejects a consumed bundle, and a revoked key is rejected before payload acceptance.

findings.title: Offline update migration execution is declared but not automatically rehearsed
findings.description: The signed update format lists migration files and validation commands, and file apply/rollback is proven, but the update engine does not execute migrations or capture a reversible database rehearsal.
findings.impact: A source update may apply successfully while its schema change fails or cannot be rolled back.
findings.recommendation: Keep migration rehearsal as a release gate for every signed update.
findings.acceptanceTest: A real previous-version database migrates, validates, rolls back, and preserves prior data.

findings.title: Root and signing keys lack protected hardware custody and rotation proof
findings.description: Context-separated keys, signing identities, validity, purpose and revocation are implemented, but root keys and private signing keys remain process memory or PEM material in the proof harness.
findings.impact: Host compromise could expose all software-protected sovereign identities and backup keys.
findings.recommendation: Implement optional OS keychain or TPM-backed adapters, rotation ceremonies, recovery-key separation, and secret-access audit.
findings.acceptanceTest: Rotate installation, tenant, backup, and signing keys without losing authorized data; revoked versions cannot sign or decrypt new material.

findings.title: Monolithic test orchestration retains an open handle after all suites report
findings.description: The complete Vitest run reports every suite as passing but does not terminate within the bounded window; split deterministic runs terminate and prove all tests.
findings.impact: CI can hang after successful tests, wasting capacity and obscuring real timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Retain isolated per-file execution as release authority and diagnose the monolithic command separately.
findings.acceptanceTest: Every discovered test file exits in a bounded child process and the aggregate gate exits zero.

findings.title: Real browser and accessibility evidence is blocked by managed navigation policy
findings.description: Authenticated Chromium tests reach the browser but every localhost navigation is rejected with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR.
findings.impact: Keyboard, focus, responsive, offline, failure-state, and screen-reader behavior cannot be promoted from contracts to runtime evidence.
findings.recommendation: Run the frozen source in a disposable browser environment without the managed deny-all URL policy; do not alter the protected host policy.
findings.acceptanceTest: Chromium and a second engine complete the sovereign workflow, accessibility scan, keyboard flow, and visual states.

findings.title: No real local generative model executed despite a complete runtime contract
findings.description: The local runtime lifecycle and candidate profile exist, but qualification found no signed model artifact and no loopback runtime endpoint.
findings.impact: Reasoning quality, structured output, tool behavior, memory use, latency, RAM, and energy remain unproven for sovereign intelligence.
findings.recommendation: Execute the hash-verified candidate or another licensed local model on the target mini-PC and run the canonical benchmark.
findings.acceptanceTest: A real local model passes quality, authorization, structured output, tool, memory, recovery, latency, and hardware thresholds.

findings.title: Portable key custody is not equivalent to OS or hardware-backed custody
findings.description: v16 separates and encrypts key purposes, but private material remains exportable after passphrase-based decryption and no TPM or OS keychain adapter was proven.
findings.impact: Filesystem or passphrase compromise can expose signing and encryption material required for high-value sovereign operation.
findings.recommendation: Implement and validate a target-platform OS keychain or hardware-backed adapter with recovery and rotation drills.
findings.acceptanceTest: Non-exportable or OS-protected keys sign, rotate, revoke, recover, and reject cross-purpose use on target hardware.

findings.title: Offline retrieval fallback has no semantic embedding comparison
findings.description: The governed BM25 fallback is local and safe, but no local embedding or reranking model was available for quality comparison.
findings.impact: Lexical retrieval may miss semantically relevant evidence or overvalue repeated terms.
findings.recommendation: Benchmark lexical, local embedding, hybrid, reranked, and disabled retrieval on a fixed sovereign task corpus.
findings.acceptanceTest: A selected strategy improves precision and task correctness without increasing unsafe-action or context-contamination rates.

findings.title: Offline installation still assumes a compatible preinstalled Node runtime
findings.description: Locked dependencies install from a verified cache without registry access, but Node and platform-level prerequisites are not included in a signed installation bundle.
findings.impact: A clean bare machine cannot yet be installed from TITAI media alone.
findings.recommendation: Create platform-specific signed runtime bundles or a verified installer manifest and prove installation on the target machine.
findings.acceptanceTest: A clean target with no public network installs the runtime, dependencies, source, migrations and application from signed media.

findings.title: Physical multi-node and long-disconnection conflict behavior remains unproven
findings.description: A separate worker process and signing identity passed capability, scope, integrity, and replay checks on one host; two physical nodes and long-disconnection conflict semantics were not exercised.
findings.impact: Network partitions, clock differences, deletion propagation, and divergent authoritative state may behave differently across machines.
findings.recommendation: Run the signed lease on the user's mini-PC or a second VM and test revocation, deadlines, stale results and conflicting offline changes.
findings.acceptanceTest: Two isolated nodes complete and reintegrate work under failure without cross-scope access or silent conflict merge.

findings.title: Energy-aware routing has no target-hardware measurement
findings.description: The current environment reports CPU and RAM but exposes no supported energy counter and is not the user's target mini-PC.
findings.impact: Energy utility values may be inaccurate and must not control model or node selection.
findings.recommendation: Measure idle, load, model startup, inference, retrieval, backup, restore and thermal behavior on the target hardware.
findings.acceptanceTest: Hardware-provenance measurements provide bounded confidence and remain advisory until thresholds are validated.

findings.title: The initial isolated test runner contained invalid JavaScript syntax
findings.description: A TypeScript non-null assertion was accidentally placed in an .mjs file, preventing the new authoritative test command from starting.
findings.impact: A release-control improvement could itself have become an unexecuted documentation claim.
findings.recommendation: Run node syntax validation for every JavaScript release script and retain the executed full-suite evidence.
findings.acceptanceTest: The corrected runner starts, executes every discovered test in a bounded child process, and exits zero.

findings.title: Physical pilot labels could be satisfied by simulated evidence
findings.description: Earlier readiness structures did not encode which gates require real hardware, browser, model, or separated-machine execution.
findings.impact: A future implementation could relabel deterministic or same-host proof as a physical pilot pass.
findings.recommendation: Enforce gate-specific execution kinds, release hashes and machine separation.
findings.acceptanceTest: Simulation, static analysis, estimates, same-host verifier and one-node records are rejected even when labeled passed.

findings.title: Offline installer archive is not yet a trusted complete artifact
findings.description: v17 can build a platform-specific staging tree with runtime, build, dependencies and migrations, but the bounded environment did not complete a trusted distributable archive and external clean-target proof.
findings.impact: A clean sovereign machine cannot yet be provisioned from one independently verified bundle.
findings.recommendation: Run the signed installer builder on a disposable target, use a trusted signing key, include separately governed browser/model artifacts, and prove install, repair and uninstall without network.
findings.acceptanceTest: A complete bundle verifies, installs, starts, restores and uninstalls on a clean target with no public network.

findings.title: Real local model benchmark remains unavailable
findings.description: The 30-case qualification lane exists but no signed GGUF artifact and loopback runtime endpoint are available.
findings.impact: Local intelligence quality, safety, throughput and energy remain unproven.
findings.recommendation: Run the signed model collector on the target Mini-PC using a hash-verified official artifact and loopback runtime.
findings.acceptanceTest: The real model meets structured-output, task-success and high-risk refusal thresholds.

findings.title: OS or hardware key custody is not executed
findings.description: The hash-pinned helper contract exists, but the current environment has no TPM device, DPAPI, or Linux Secret Service backend.
findings.impact: High-value signing and encryption keys remain protected only by the portable encrypted fallback.
findings.recommendation: Execute a reviewed hash-pinned custody helper on the target OS and prove rotation, revocation, recovery and wrong-purpose denial.
findings.acceptanceTest: At least one OS or hardware backend passes all custody tests and is shown in the UI.

findings.title: Browser policy prevents real UI and accessibility proof
findings.description: The managed Chromium environment applies URLBlocklist star and prevents loopback navigation.
findings.impact: Golden workflow, keyboard, focus, screen-reader, responsive, offline and visual evidence are unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Run the signed browser collector in an unrestricted disposable environment using Playwright-managed browser artifacts.
findings.acceptanceTest: Chromium and a secondary engine complete the workflow with no critical accessibility failure.

findings.title: Two-machine execution remains unproven
findings.description: Only one privacy-preserving machine fingerprint was collected; same-host process separation cannot prove physical node independence.
findings.impact: Node trust, failure isolation and external verification remain vulnerable to common-host failure and hidden shared state.
findings.recommendation: Collect signed profiles and execute a scoped task across two distinct machines or separately administered hosts.
findings.acceptanceTest: Two distinct fingerprints pass registration, task binding, replay, revocation, failure and reintegration checks.

findings.title: Drizzle dependency versions were stale and unvalidated
findings.description: The repository previously retained drizzle-orm 0.44.6 and drizzle-kit 0.31.5 because real candidate artifacts had not been acquired and tested.
findings.impact: The release carried a known dependency-upgrade blocker and could not claim current migration-tool validation.
findings.recommendation: Acquire exact candidate artifacts, record integrity, update lockfile and run all behavioral gates.
findings.acceptanceTest: drizzle-orm 0.45.2 and drizzle-kit 0.31.10 pass typecheck, migrations, persistence tests and production build with rollback material preserved.

findings.title: Control plane previously treated same-host isolated execution as multi-node proof
findings.description: The default control-plane snapshot marked multiNodeExecution true based on separate-process evidence from one host.
findings.impact: Operators could infer physical failure isolation that had not been established.
findings.recommendation: Default multi-node readiness to blocked until two distinct machine fingerprints are verified.
findings.acceptanceTest: The default control plane reports multi-node blocked while preserving full-suite clean-exit truth.

findings.title: Foundry candidates were initially ephemeral across process restart
findings.description: The first v18 Foundry API generated capability candidates in memory without a canonical persistent record.
findings.impact: Operator work could disappear after refresh or restart, and candidate state could not be audited durably.
findings.recommendation: Persist candidates with tenant, workspace, owner, specification hash, candidate hash and lifecycle state.
findings.acceptanceTest: SQLite proof shows idempotent candidate persistence, restart-safe records and cross-scope isolation.

findings.title: Capability timestamp column mapping drift could break runtime registry reads
findings.description: A generic timestamp helper mapped importedAt and installedAt to created_at while the migration created imported_at and installed_at.
findings.impact: The registry could pass TypeScript yet fail at runtime on real SQLite queries.
findings.recommendation: Map physical column names explicitly and add a schema contract regression test.
findings.acceptanceTest: The schema test verifies imported_at, installed_at and created_at names and the real SQLite persistence proof passes.

findings.title: Restricted Node subprocess is not a hostile-code security boundary
findings.description: The v18 restricted subprocess applies static checks, filtered environment, timeout and output ceilings, but does not prove kernel-enforced filesystem, process, memory or network isolation against malicious native or runtime escape behavior.
findings.impact: Activating arbitrary untrusted packages could expose host files, secrets or network access beyond the declared manifest.
findings.recommendation: Keep high-risk and untrusted package classes disabled until an OS, WASI, container or remote disposable sandbox is independently proven.
findings.acceptanceTest: A hostile package suite cannot escape filesystem, process, environment, memory or network limits under an independently observed isolation boundary.

findings.title: Monolithic Vitest remains unreliable as the authoritative release command
findings.description: The all-in-one Vitest process can report completed assertions while retaining an open handle or exceeding the execution window.
findings.impact: A green assertion summary may not prove deterministic teardown or a clean release process.
findings.recommendation: Retain the isolated per-file runner as release authority and continue diagnosing the monolithic handle leak.
findings.acceptanceTest: The authoritative isolated runner executes every test file in a separate bounded process with zero failures and zero timeouts; the monolithic command later exits cleanly as an additional gate.

findings.title: Capability publisher key is proof custody rather than production custody
findings.description: The v18 package publisher identity is generated for the evidence run and proves signing semantics, but it is not protected by OS or hardware-backed production custody.
findings.impact: The controlled subsystem package can be verified, but publisher compromise resistance and operational rotation are not production-proven.
findings.recommendation: Move publisher signing to the approved OS or hardware custody backend and preserve revocation and recovery evidence.
findings.acceptanceTest: A non-exportable or OS-protected publisher key signs, rotates and revokes packages on the target installation without plaintext private-key exposure.

findings.title: Self-improvement proof is a controlled lifecycle model, not autonomous patch execution
findings.description: v18 proves proposal freezing, role separation, evidence gates, canary and rollback state transitions, but the proof does not autonomously edit and validate an arbitrary repository worktree.
findings.impact: The safety control plane is implemented, while broad self-hosted code improvement remains less mature than the product label may imply.
findings.recommendation: Retain bounded wording and require a future real worktree patch experiment before claiming general self-improvement.
findings.acceptanceTest: A weakness discovered from raw evidence is patched in an isolated worktree, independently tested, canaried and rolled back using the same pipeline.

findings.title: Capability OS browser and accessibility workflow is not physically verified
findings.description: The Capability OS UI, Mission Studio and Foundry surfaces compile and have contract tests, but browser E2E, keyboard, accessibility and responsive behavior remain blocked by the managed browser environment.
findings.impact: Operator usability and accessibility cannot be promoted from static or source evidence alone.
findings.recommendation: Run the v17 physical browser collector against the v18 routes in an unmanaged disposable browser environment.
findings.acceptanceTest: Chromium and a secondary engine complete the Capability Foundry workflow with accessibility, keyboard and visual-regression evidence.

findings.title: Subsystem verifier remains same-host process separation rather than external-host independence
findings.description: The v18 verifier is an evidence-only separate process with a separate Ed25519 identity, but it runs on the same execution host.
findings.impact: The subsystem release decision is cryptographically bound and conflict-separated, yet common-host compromise and hidden environment dependence are not excluded.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the final verifier bundle on a separately administered host or VM and compare the resulting attestation.
findings.acceptanceTest: A distinct host fingerprint independently extracts the final ZIP, verifies all files and package signatures, reruns required gates and signs the same decision.
